chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Hatam, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

I saw that good deeds (al-ma'ruf) are not perfected except by three qualities: diminishing them, concealing them, and hastening them. For if you diminish them, they become greater in the eyes of the one to whom you do the favor; and if you conceal them, you perfect them; and if you hasten them, you bring them joy. And if it is otherwise, you diminish their value and cause annoyance.

key_terms.الْمَعْرُوف: Good deeds or acts of kindness
key_terms.عَظَمْتَهُ: You make it great (in the eyes of the recipient)

ai.seo_question: What are the three qualities that perfect good deeds according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the etiquette of giving by emphasizing humility, privacy, and promptness as essential components of *al-ma'ruf*. This triad ensures the recipient's dignity is preserved and the act is spiritually accepted, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) and *haya* (modesty) in social interactions. Neglecting these nuances transforms a charitable act into a source of social friction, highlighting the interplay between intention and execution in Islamic ethics.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-143 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sa’dan ibn Muslim, on the authority of Hatam that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

Good deeds will not be perfected unless youdo the following three acts: underestimate them, cover them up, and expedite them. They will be well-noticed by those to whom you do a favour once you underestimate them. They will be perfected when you cover them up. And they will be enjoyed by those to whom you do the favour if you expedite them. Otherwise, you would spoil them.”
